claims.text: The opportunity provides tuition fee support of up to £1,820 per year.
The opportunity is for eligible undergraduate students.
The opportunity is for students studying at Scottish universities or colleges.
The opportunity is for individuals from low-income households.
The opportunity is for individuals ineligible for tuition fee support from the Scottish Government.
The opportunity supports students enrolled on an undergraduate degree course at a Scottish Institute of Higher Education.
The opportunity covers the cost of tuition fees.
Applicants must demonstrate that their financial circumstances do not allow them to cover the cost of their tuition fees.
Retrospective applications will not be accepted.
Applications will not be accepted if the student has incurred tuition fee debts in a previous year of study and is unable to move to the next level of their course as a result.
Applicants must live in a low-income household.

Applicants must be ordinarily resident in Scotland at the time of applying and have completed at least two full years of secondary schooling or college education in Scotland, OR be able to demonstrate a substantial and recent connection to Scotland.
Applicants must be entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK, have Limited Leave to Remain under a visa valid for the entire duration of the course, or be an asylum seeker.
Applicants must not be eligible for public funds (e.g. grants or loans) towards the cost of tuition fees.
Applicants must not have already graduated with a university degree.
Applicants eligible for a SAAS/Student Loans Company maintenance loan are expected to take full advantage of the loans available.

The fund will not consider an application if the student is eligible for support (including loans) from Student Finance England, Wales or Northern Ireland, or any loan or grant from an overseas government or agency.
In general, the fund will not fund more than one repeat year for the same course and student.
Applications from students who previously received funding for an undergraduate degree and wish to start a different course may not be considered.
Part-time students in receipt of tuition fee support from SAAS may apply if the amount awarded by SAAS is less than the total amount of fees payable.
Students who came to Scotland to study at university or college but have no experience of education in Scotland before that, and no other ties to Scotland, will not be considered eligible.
Applications from students who already have a university degree level qualification may be considered exceptionally at the discretion of the fund.

Applicants must have an unconditional offer for, or be a continuing student on, a full-time, part-time or distance learning undergraduate degree course in academic year 2026-27 at a listed Scottish institution or a course validated by a listed university.
HNC and HND diploma courses are not eligible for support.
Access courses are not eligible for support.
Accelerated degree courses with a graduate entry are not eligible for support.
Courses delivered by, or at, a university outside Scotland are not eligible for support.
Courses at a Scottish Higher Education Institute delivered and validated by a university outside Scotland are not eligible for support.
Open University courses are not eligible for support.
Continuing Professional Development (CPD) courses are not eligible for support.
University courses below degree level are not eligible for support.
Postgraduate degrees are not eligible for support.
The fund has a budget to fund students who completed an undergraduate degree in the past and wish to start an undergraduate degree in a different field of study in academic year 2026-27.
Students seeking to reskill in a different field of study after a previous degree must have completed their first degree at least two years before the start of their new course.
Students seeking to reskill must enter the first year of their course in academic year 2026-27.
Students seeking to reskill must have been unable to gain employment in the subject area of their previous degree, are unemployed, have been made redundant or are facing redundancy.
Students seeking to reskill must wish to reskill in a different field of study, unrelated to their previous qualifications and recognised as being in a skills shortage area for the Scottish economy.
Applications are processed on a first come first served basis.
The awards cover tuition fees only, up to a maximum of £1,820.
The fund considers household income and other extenuating circumstances.
The application portal will be open from June 1, 2026, to 5 pm on December 1, 2026, for grants covering academic year 2026-27.
Applicants must complete an eligibility checker before applying.

Late applications after the closing date will not be accepted, unless the student can demonstrate they were first informed that SAAS would not be covering their fees after the online portal has closed.
Applicants will be notified of the outcome of their applications within two to three weeks.
Supporting documents include evidence of applicant eligibility, letter of acceptance for the university course, SAAS Award Notice letter, and P60 or pay slips/Universal Credit statements.
Students who have already started a 2nd degree before academic year 2026-27 are not eligible to apply.
